# Relapsing polychondritis

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Rheumatology and immunology > Connective tissue diseases > Relapsing polychondritis*

[Original Article Link](/library/_80563)

---

## Summary

Relapsing polychondritis is a rare inflammatory disease with an autoimmune component characterized by <u>chondritis</u> (e.g., auricular, nasal, and/or laryngotracheobronchial) with or without systemic involvement (e.g., <u>arthropathy</u>, <u>episcleritis</u>, and/or <u>valvular heart disease</u>). Laryngotracheobronchial <u>chondritis</u> is the most common cause of mortality in relapsing polychondritis and may necessitate emergency interventions (e.g., <u>tracheostomy</u>). Relapsing polychondritis is sometimes associated with other conditions (e.g., <u>systemic lupus erythematosus</u>, <u>ANCA-associated vasculitis</u>, and solid organ cancers). Diagnosis is clinical and often delayed due to variable manifestations and insidious onset. A comprehensive diagnostic evaluation is used to rule out alternative diagnoses (e.g., autoimmune diseases) and assess for systemic involvement (e.g., <u>laryngotracheobronchitis</u>, <u>valvular heart disease</u>). Treatment aims to control <u>acute inflammation</u> and prevent long-term damage. Mild disease is managed with <u>NSAIDs</u> or <u>dapsone</u>. Severe disease (e.g., severe polychondritis and/or laryngotracheobronchial involvement) is treated with <u>systemic glucocorticoids</u>. <u>Conventional DMARDs</u> and <u>biologic DMARDs</u> may be used in refractory disease. Long-term complications of <u>chondritis</u> include audiovestibular symptoms, <u>ear</u> deformity, and <u>saddle nose deformity</u>.
